description:
We are seeking a Software Engineer (SWE) – Level 1 to support mission-critical Government programs focused on software development, system integration, application modernization, and advanced computing solutions.
 The ideal candidate will possess a foundational understanding of software engineering principles, programming methodologies, and system architecture. This position involves designing, developing, testing, and maintaining complex software systems supporting data-intensive analytics, algorithm development, real-time processing, and enterprise applications.
 The Software Engineer will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams to translate technical requirements into functional software solutions, troubleshoot existing applications, and enhance system performance, reliability, and scalability in support of Government mission objectives.
 Active US Security Clearance w/ Polygraph 
 Key Responsibilities
 Analyze user requirements and translate functional and technical specifications into software design and performance requirements.
 Design, develop, test, and maintain software applications and components supporting complex Government systems and operational environments.
 Write, debug, and optimize software code to correct defects, improve functionality, and implement new features.
 Integrate existing software applications and components into new or modified systems, platforms, and operating environments.
 Support the development and maintenance of software systems involving large-scale data processing, real-time applications, analytics, and algorithm development.
 Develop and execute software tests to validate functionality, performance, and compliance with established design requirements.
 Document software test results, troubleshoot reported issues, and implement corrective actions to improve system reliability.
 Develop basic database queries to retrieve, manipulate, and analyze information from existing or proposed databases and data repositories.
 Participate in software design reviews and provide technical input on software reuse, system integration, and Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) or Government Off-the-Shelf (GOTS) solutions.
 Collaborate with software engineers, system architects, and technical stakeholders to evaluate hardware/software trade-offs and support system-level design decisions.
 Maintain technical documentation, software design specifications, and development procedures while recommending improvements to software engineering processes.
 Apply appropriate software development methodologies, coding standards, and configuration management practices throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC).
 
 Requirements 
 Required Qualifications
 Seven (7) years experience as a SWE, in programs and contracts of similar scope, type, and complexity is required.
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical discipline from an accredited college or university. Four (4) years of software engineering experience on projects utilizing similar software processes may be substituted for the degree.
 Foundational knowledge of software engineering principles, programming concepts, and object-oriented or procedural software development.
 Familiarity with at least one programming language, such as Java, Python, C, C++, or C#.
 Understanding of software debugging, testing, troubleshooting, and defect resolution methodologies.
 Basic knowledge of database concepts, data structures, algorithms, and software integration principles.
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to work independently or collaboratively within a technical team.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience or academic exposure to developing applications using Java, Python, C++, C#, or other modern programming languages.
 Familiarity with Agile software development methodologies, version control systems such as Git, and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) practices.
 Knowledge of relational or nonrelational databases, SQL queries, and data processing techniques.
 Exposure to Linux or Windows development environments, software testing frameworks, and application integration.
 Familiarity with Department of Defense (DoD) or Intelligence Community (IC) software engineering environments, including secure development practices and mission-focused applications.
